The marker result is not a historical-unit false positive. Although journalctl was queried by reused unit name without an invocation boundary and the shorter OFF logs therefore also contain old R1 PIDs, every one of the 4,026 exact markers is tied to the current R2 ON PIDs 140155 or 140280. The two current OFF PID spans are retained from startup through idle completion and contain no marker. The method should nevertheless be hardened to query the current invocation or PID because unrestricted unit history is an avoidable contamination risk.

The stored trace_verbosity_verified=false is a preregistered evidence-gate failure but also an observability false negative for effective launch configuration. Contrary to the supplied shorthand that only b1 retained the declaration, direct current-PID inspection finds the exact startup declaration in b1_off and b4_off, but not b2_on or b3_on: two of four journals satisfy the literal requirement. Both ON files contain exactly the journalctl -n 20000 cap and begin about four seconds into execution amid trace-level graph records, whereas the compact OFF files retain startup. The common -lv 4 argv is independently captured for all four live processes, and the trace-only instrumented marker itself is emitted thousands of times in both ON blocks. Thus the missing declarations are best explained by tail truncation, not by -lv 4 being absent.

Fail-closed promotion is still illegal. The preregistration says every journal must contain the startup declaration and separately lists absent trace-verbosity declaration as an abort condition. The R2 wrapper calls the complete R1 execution first, captures journals only after requests with journalctl -n 20000, and evaluates the declaration only afterward; it therefore could not enforce the frozen abort before collecting scientific requests. Neither argv evidence nor marker presence may retroactively replace the expressly frozen per-journal positive control.

The marker separation is positive evidence that the instrumented Qwen3.8 runtime observed the gated-delta-net fused-cache matcher under the ON environment and not under the OFF environment in these blocks. It does not measure speed, cache-write reduction, production readiness, deployment status or generalization, and the 16/16 output equality is only exact parity on the eight fixed prompts across two crossover pairs. No timing or hardware field is accepted as a performance endpoint.

The R2 exact-file ledger fixes the R1 semantic-hash defect. Fresh byte counts and SHA-256 values for samples.jsonl (72,269 bytes/ca18d4c89781827523286b0b014ad066874cc08dae4a0d5f11b51140a36754a5), paired_metrics.json (4,813 bytes/605e3f8a0f086279ef0401bc84ee8199bb1cf2a7650503dcfe3fae907ca4808b) and blocks.jsonl (29,769 bytes/3c75a284b3e0cf98858b06bfe913c978ecc3909d3a0e95f76ed6b6050e43467d) exactly match end_to_end_artifact.json and receipt provenance.

Service restoration passes. The persistent gateway was stopped through systemd, qwen38 was restored healthy under the same gateway command, the final service is active/running with zero restarts, and embedding remained HTTP 200. Fresh read-only checks reproduce restored PID 140533, active/running state, qwen38 backend health and HTTP 200 on both 8080 and 8081.

The admissible disposition is REJECTED with bounded claim SLX03_GDN_FUSION_RUNTIME_ROUTE_NOT_CONFIRMED_R2 because one frozen acceptance gate failed and its associated abort control was not implemented prospectively. This rejects the preregistered package, not the physical marker observation. A minimal successor should keep the same identities, ABBA order, prompts and claim limits, start each fresh unit with -lv 4, immediately capture and hash the current invocation's startup segment before any warmup or request, require the declaration there, then collect a separately invocation-bounded request journal without a lossy tail cap. It must again require ON/OFF marker separation, exact paired output equality and service restoration. No speed, write-reduction, deployment or non-Qwen3.8 claim is authorized.
